[Shop online](https://www.royalcollectionshop.co.uk/) ### Refreshments Eating and drinking are not permitted inside The King's Gallery, except for bottled water. You will be asked to place drinks and food in closed bags before being admitted. Food and drink are not available for purchase at the Gallery, but there are many cafés and restaurants in the local area. We offer a range of interactive workshops, tours, learning activities and resources for nursery, primary and secondary pupils. Our [school visit information](https://www.rct.uk/schools/school-visits/essential-visit-information/the-kings-gallery-buckingham-palace) will help teachers and organisers plan their visit. ### School sessions School session #### [From Palace to Planet: Sustainable fashion workshop for Key Stage 2](https://www.rct.uk/schools/sessions/from-palace-to-planet-sustainable-fashion-workshop-for-key-stage-2 'From Palace to Planet: Sustainable fashion workshop for Key Stage 2') - The King's Gallery, Buckingham Palace - 12 Apr 2026 - 15 Apr 2027 - Key stage 2 - Art & Design, Design & Technology, History - Changes within living memory, Coronation, Drawing techniques, Famous people, Fashion, Kings and Queens, Lives of significant individuals, Materials, Materials and their uses, Monarchy, Patterns, Symbolism School session #### [From Palace to Planet: Sustainable fashion workshop for Key Stage 3](https://www.rct.uk/schools/sessions/from-palace-to-planet-sustainable-fashion-workshop-for-key-stage-3 'From Palace to Planet: Sustainable fashion workshop for Key Stage 3') - The King's Gallery, Buckingham Palace - 12 Apr 2026 - 15 Apr 2027 - Key stage 3, Key stage 4 - Art & Design, Design & Technology, History - Architects & Designers, Chronology, Communication language and literacy, Critical understanding of artists, Drawing techniques, Fashion, Historical Interpretation, Materials, Materials and their uses, Monarchy, Patterns, Pioneers, Symbolism [View all school sessions in London](https://www.rct.uk/schools/sessions/london) [Back to top](https://www.rct.uk/visit/the-kings-gallery-buckingham-palace#section-jump-menu) ## Access and mobility The King's Gallery is accessible. Concessionary rates are available if you have a disability and we offer a free access companion ticket which can be booked online. No proof of disability is required. Limited seating is available.  Registered assistance dogs are welcome. The Gallery comprises three large exhibition rooms and a number of smaller spaces. You may wish to [download a photo journey (PDF)](https://cmsadmin.rct.uk/sites/default/files/2026-04/KG_Her%20Life%20in%20Style%20-%20Access%20Guide_Photo%20Journey_2026.pdf) to help you plan your visit. Visitors to the exhibition can watch an introductory video when they first enter. If you would like to experience the film in your own time or space you can watch the [introductory video from the exhibition _Queen Elizabeth II: Her Life in Style_](https://www.rct.uk/resources/introductory-video-from-the-exhibition-queen-elizabeth-ii-her-life-in-style). There is no café or parking on-site, but both are available nearby. General information on visiting is available on our [Practical Information page](https://www.rct.uk/visit/the-queens-gallery-buckingham-palace/practical-information#/). For detailed access information, please select one of the options below. For any other information, you can contact the Specialist Sales team on +44 (0)303 123 7324 or by emailing [specialistsales@rct.uk](mailto:specialistsales@rct.uk?subject=Visiting%20The%20Queen's%20Gallery%2C%20Buckingham%20Palace).  [Mobility access logo](https://www.rct.uk/visit/the-queens-gallery-buckingham-palace/mobility-access) [Mobility access](https://www.rct.uk/visit/the-queens-gallery-buckingham-palace/mobility-access) [D/deaf or hard of hearing logo](https://www.rct.uk/visit/the-queens-gallery-buckingham-palace/ddeaf-or-hard-of-hearing) [D/deaf or hard of hearing](https://www.rct.uk/visit/the-queens-gallery-buckingham-palace/ddeaf-or-hard-of-hearing) [Blind or partially-sighted logo](https://www.rct.uk/visit/the-queens-gallery-buckingham-palace/blind-or-partially-sighted) [Blind or partially-sighted](https://www.rct.uk/visit/the-queens-gallery-buckingham-palace/blind-or-partially-sighted) [Autism spectrum logo](https://www.rct.uk/visit/the-kings-gallery-buckingham-palace/neurodivergent-visitors-at-the-kings-gallery) [Neurodivergent Visitors](https://www.rct.uk/visit/the-kings-gallery-buckingham-palace/neurodivergent-visitors-at-the-kings-gallery) ### Access events Online lecture ### [Descriptive Zoom talks for blind & partially-sighted people](https://www.rct.uk/event/descriptive-zooms 'Descriptive Zoom talks for blind & partially-sighted people') - The exhibition features clothing worn in all ten decades of her life - from birth to adulthood, from princess to queen, and from off-duty style to dressing for momentous occasions in Britain’s history. 2026 price 2027 price Adult £22.00 £24.00 Young Person (18-24) £14.00 £15.50 Child (5-17) £11.00 £12.00 Disabled Person £11.00 £12.00 Access companion Free Free Under 5 Free Free Show all prices [Book nowticket for](https://tickets.rct.uk/product/11/6996) ### Royal Jewellery: From Coronations to Keepsakes 25 Jun 2027 - 19 Mar 2028 Explore 500 years of British royal jewellery worn by monarchs from Henry VIII and Charles II to Queen Victoria and Queen Elizabeth II. The exhibition follows the story of royal jewellery, from the work of early royal goldsmiths to designs by famous jewellery houses such as Garrard & Co, Cartier, Boucheron and Fabergé. Discover how jewellery has helped shape the image of the monarchy over the centuries.
